actions.name: Camera inspection of oral cavity/oropharynx
actions.result: Oral cavity and oropharynx: no visible mucosal lesions, no obvious masses, poor dentition noted, tongue mobile and symmetric, tonsils absent (prior tonsillectomy per patient). Limited view of hypopharynx/larynx as expected on unaided camera exam.

actions.name: Camera inspection of neck
actions.result: Right-sided neck swelling visible at level II, approximately 2 cm, patient reports it is non-tender; no visible skin changes, no obvious asymmetry of thyroid cartilage on external exam.

actions.name: Patient self-palpation of neck mass (guided)
actions.result: Patient reports a firm, non-mobile, non-tender lump below the right jaw angle, approximately 2 cm, present for about 3 weeks, not changing with swallowing.

actions.name: Cranial nerve screening exam (facial symmetry, tongue protrusion, shoulder shrug) via camera
actions.result: Facial movement symmetric, tongue protrudes midline, shoulder shrug strong and symmetric bilaterally, no voice change with phonation beyond baseline hoarseness.

actions.name: Review home/office vitals
actions.result: BP 132/80 mmHg, HR 78 bpm, SpO2 97% on room air, weight 61 kg (down from 65 kg three months ago), BMI 23.

actions.name: Order flexible fiberoptic laryngoscopy (in-person, urgent referral)
actions.result: Scheduling order placed for urgent in-person flexible laryngoscopy within 1 week; patient instructed on what to expect; visit cannot substitute for direct visualization of the larynx.

actions.name: Order contrast-enhanced CT neck/soft tissue
actions.result: Order placed for CT neck with contrast to evaluate laryngeal mass extent and cervical lymphadenopathy; to be obtained prior to or same day as laryngoscopy if possible.

actions.name: Order chest imaging to screen for synchronous primary/metastasis
actions.result: No prior chest imaging on file; order placed for chest x-ray or CT chest to screen for a synchronous lung primary or metastatic disease given smoking history, to be coordinated with oncology once a primary site is confirmed; full staging determination will require multidisciplinary input.

actions.name: Review urgent care visit note (prior antibiotic/PPI trial)
actions.result: Urgent care note from 7 weeks ago: diagnosed 'laryngitis, possible reflux,' prescribed azithromycin 5-day course and omeprazole 40 mg daily x4 weeks. No laryngoscopy performed. Note documents 'denies dysphagia at time of visit.' Patient reports no improvement in voice since.

actions.name: Review smoking/alcohol history documentation in chart
actions.result: Social history (prior primary care note, 8 months ago): tobacco use documented as 1 pack/day x40 years (40 pack-year history); alcohol use recorded as 'social drinker only, denies heavy use.' No subsequent chart update on alcohol use is on file.

actions.name: Voice/perceptual assessment (listen to sustained phonation and reading passage over video)
actions.result: Voice is persistently rough/breathy with reduced loudness and shortened maximum phonation time (~8 seconds); no stridor at rest.

actions.name: Screen for airway distress (ask about breathing, observe respiratory effort on camera)
actions.result: No stridor, no use of accessory muscles, respiratory rate 16, patient denies shortness of breath or noisy breathing at rest or with exertion.

actions.name: Review CBC
actions.result: WBC 7.2 x10^9/L (4.0-11.0), Hgb 12.6 g/dL (12.0-15.5), Platelets 240 x10^9/L (150-400) - all within normal limits; mild anemia risk flagged for monitoring given weight loss but currently normal.

actions.name: Review prior primary care social history note
actions.result: Social history (8 months ago): tobacco use - current smoker, 1 pack/day since age 20 (40 pack-year history), advised cessation multiple times, not ready to quit. Alcohol - 'social drinker only, denies heavy use.' Occupation: school bus dispatcher, works via two-way radio most of shift.

answerKey.primaryProblem: Suspected laryngeal (or hypopharyngeal) squamous cell carcinoma presenting as persistent hoarseness with red-flag features (otalgia, dysphagia, weight loss, neck mass) in a heavy smoker/drinker, requiring urgent laryngoscopy and staging workup; outside the scope of a telehealth visit to diagnose definitively.
differential: Laryngeal or hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma
Vocal cord lesion (polyp, nodule, papilloma) less likely given systemic red flags
Chronic laryngitis/LPR (prior diagnosis, now insufficient given lack of response and red flags)
Reactive or metastatic cervical lymphadenopathy from head/neck primary
Thyroid mass with secondary voice change (TSH normal, less likely primary)
keyFindings: Hoarseness >6 weeks unresponsive to antibiotic/PPI trial, mandating laryngoscopy per guidelines
Referred right otalgia (classic for hypopharyngeal/laryngeal lesion via vagal referral)
Unintentional weight loss of approximately 4 kg over 3 months (~6.2% of body weight, meeting criteria for clinically significant unintentional weight loss)
New right neck mass, firm, non-tender, non-mobile, ~2 cm, present ~3 weeks
40 pack-year smoking history and heavy nightly alcohol use (synergistic carcinogen risk)
No airway compromise currently (no stridor, normal SpO2 and respiratory effort)
plan: Urgent in-person flexible fiberoptic laryngoscopy within days, not deferred for repeat medication trial
Contrast-enhanced CT of the neck to characterize laryngeal/hypopharyngeal lesion and cervical nodal disease
Chest imaging (CXR or CT chest) for synchronous lung primary/staging given smoking history
If mass confirmed on laryngoscopy or imaging, biopsy and multidisciplinary head and neck tumor board referral
Counsel on smoking and alcohol cessation resources regardless of final diagnosis
Set expectations: diagnosis cannot be confirmed by video exam alone; same-week in-person evaluation is essential
Address patient's fear (husband's lung cancer death) with clear, honest communication about next steps and timeline
redFlags: Hoarseness persisting beyond 2 weeks without improvement after empiric therapy (ACR/AAO-HNS indication for laryngoscopy)
Unintentional weight loss (~6.2% body weight over 3 months)
Palpable, firm, non-tender, enlarging neck mass
Heavy combined tobacco and alcohol exposure
educationPoints: Persistent hoarseness >2-3 weeks, especially with any red flag, requires direct laryngeal visualization regardless of empiric treatment trials already given
Referred otalgia with normal ear exam should prompt evaluation of the aerodigestive tract (cranial nerves IX/X referral pathways)
Combined tobacco and heavy alcohol use multiplies head and neck cancer risk beyond either alone
A telehealth visit can triage and expedite urgent in-person procedures but cannot replace direct laryngoscopy or tissue diagnosis
Patients may minimize alcohol use initially ('socially') and disclose more accurately once rapport is established-screen directly and gently
Unintentional weight loss (here, ~6.2% of body weight in 3 months) and new neck mass in a smoker are not to be attributed to reflux or minor infection without ruling out malignancy first

artifacts.author: Dr. R. Finch, Urgent Care
artifacts.body: CC: Hoarse voice x4 weeks. HPI: 60F with hoarseness, denies fever, denies dysphagia at time of visit. Exam: oropharynx mildly erythematous, no exudate. Assessment: Acute laryngitis, possible laryngopharyngeal reflux. Plan: Azithromycin 250mg day1 then 250mg daily x4 days; Omeprazole 40mg daily x4 weeks; voice rest advised; follow up if not improved in 2-3 weeks. No laryngoscopy performed at this visit.

mismatches.patientClaim: Patient initially states she only drinks socially and denies heavy alcohol use.
mismatches.recordEvidence: Prior primary care note from 8 months ago documents 'social drinker only, denies heavy use,' matching her initial statement today. No prior record documents any heavier use, so the chart alone cannot resolve whether this is accurate.
mismatches.teachingPoint: Prior charted social history may simply reflect what the patient reported previously, not the truth; a single prior note stating 'social drinking' does not rule out underreporting, and direct, non-judgmental re-screening at this visit is essential, especially when alcohol is a major risk factor for the suspected diagnosis.

mismatches.patientClaim: Patient reports no dysphagia symptoms were present when she first saw urgent care, only hoarseness.
mismatches.recordEvidence: Urgent care note explicitly documents 'denies dysphagia at time of visit' 7 weeks ago, consistent with progression of symptoms, confirming dysphagia is a newer development not present at initial presentation.
mismatches.teachingPoint: Symptom progression (new dysphagia, weight loss, neck mass appearing after initial presentation) is itself a red flag indicating this is not resolving laryngitis but a progressive process requiring urgent re-evaluation, not just repeating the same empiric treatment.

objectives.text: Elicit the full constellation of head and neck cancer red-flag symptoms (otalgia, dysphagia, weight loss, neck mass) beyond the presenting complaint of hoarseness through structured, tiered questioning.
Recognize that hoarseness persisting beyond empiric antibiotic/PPI therapy for 6-8 weeks mandates direct laryngoscopy rather than further medication trials, and place the appropriate urgent referral.
Obtain an accurate tobacco and alcohol history, recognizing that initial patient disclosure may understate alcohol use, and connect combined use to head and neck cancer risk.
Perform a feasible remote assessment of airway safety and voice quality to determine urgency and triage appropriately without underestimating or overestimating acuity.
Order appropriate staging imaging (contrast neck CT, chest imaging) and recognize the limits of telehealth evaluation in confirming a tissue diagnosis.
Address the psychosocial dimension of the visit, including the patient's fear related to her husband's cancer death and her delay in seeking care, with empathy while maintaining urgency of workup.

patient.name: Patricia Lawson
patient.appearance: A woman who appears her age with a sturdy build, short gray-blonde hair, wearing a cardigan over a work polo shirt, seated at a kitchen table with a coffee mug visible. Lighting is a bit dim, and she speaks with a noticeably rough, raspy voice, occasionally touching the right side of her neck as she talks.

persona.personality: Chatty, warm, deflects from difficult topics with humor or small talk, but underneath is quite anxious
persona.communicationStyle: Talks in a roundabout way, volunteers unrelated details about work and family before circling back to health concerns, uses plain lay language
persona.emotionalState: Anxious beneath a cheerful exterior, especially fearful of cancer given her husband's death
persona.background: Married for 32 years to a long-haul truck driver who died of lung cancer two years ago; has two grown children who live out of state; has worked as a school bus dispatcher for 15 years and takes pride in rarely missing work despite being short-staffed
speechExamples: Oh honey, let me tell you about my week before we get into all this.
It's probably nothing, I'm sure, but my voice just won't quit being scratchy.
I don't like to make a fuss, but my neck's got this little lump that's bothering me.
After Jerry passed from the lung cancer, I guess I get spooked easier than I used to.
concerns: Worried this could be cancer like what her husband had
Worried about missing work and losing income if this requires procedures
Concerned about insurance approval delays for tests
Embarrassed about her drinking and smoking habits

scenario.studentBrief: You are the ENT resident seeing Patricia Lawson, a 60-year-old school bus dispatcher, for a new telehealth consultation regarding 8 weeks of hoarseness that has not improved despite antibiotics and a PPI trial from urgent care. Conduct a focused history, perform feasible camera-based exam maneuvers, and determine next steps.
scenario.chiefComplaint: Persistent hoarse voice for 8 weeks, not improved with antibiotics and acid reflux medication
scenario.openingLine: Hi there, thanks for seeing me. My voice has just been so scratchy and rough for about two months now, and nothing they've given me has helped one bit.
tasks: Take a focused history of the presenting concern
Obtain a tobacco and alcohol history
Perform a feasible camera-based examination of the oropharynx and neck
Determine and communicate the next steps in management
Address the patient's concerns with empathy

profile.setting: Telehealth video visit, patient at home at her kitchen table
profile.summary: A 60-year-old smoker and heavy drinker presents by telehealth with 8 weeks of hoarseness unresponsive to empiric antibiotic/PPI therapy, with red-flag features of referred otalgia, dysphagia, weight loss, and a new neck mass. The case teaches ENT residents to recognize when hoarseness requires urgent laryngoscopy and staging imaging rather than further empiric treatment, and to elicit sensitive substance use history that the patient initially minimizes.
profile.title: Persistent Hoarseness with Red Flags in a 60-Year-Old Smoker: Suspected Laryngeal Malignancy
